conclusions: Both perf and strace pairs ran original release ELFs main0846/preddca. All four daemon windows returned zero and passed the existing methodology/behavior checks. No trace replaced any primary window.

Perf captured 181 main and 321 fix hardware cycles samples, zero lost samples. Exact period-weighted kernel fractions are 74.3834% and 71.6006%; all userspace samples remain unresolved names. Sparse samples and frequency-adjusted weights do not establish a per-query kernel-cost cause.
Perf fix samples include fput/poll_freewait/do_sys_poll and sock_poll, motivating syscall-count verification; syscall evidence does not show duplicated poll/receive/send work.

Full strace attach covers 2500 warmup + 7500 measured correct requests per side. ppoll is 10089 versus10097 (1.0089 versus1.0097 per correct); mean nfds25.72693 versus25.72665, both max26. recvfrom and sendto each exactly1 per correct, accept4/close each0.01. EAGAIN/EINTR/zero-ready ppoll absent.

The unchanged strace -s0 abbreviation retains nfds but hides individual ppoll arrays. Listener fd7 and accepted TCP fds12..31 are established by accept4/getsockname/recvfrom/sendto; other poll descriptor roles cannot be reconstructed from this trace. Pure userspace cache iteration cannot be measured by strace.
Symbol companions were rejected: source rebuilds with symbols have unequal .text/ALLOC bytes. They were never substituted for original release ELFs or used to assign source functions to original IPs.

An initial perf text parser omitted user frames and an unsupported perf-script option failed during offline analysis; both failed derived artifacts remain, and corrected --hide-call-graph output matches report sample/period totals.
next_step_scope: A+B cache/local-lookup cleanup is a separately reviewed source change; subsequent three-way long windows can assess its combined effect but not attribute each cleanup individually.
